title: The horse Bayard.
lines: This is a very old story from Flanders.
It's about a horse and four brothers.
Long ago there lived four brothers.
Their names were Reinout, Adelaert, Ritsaert and Writsaert.
The four sons of Aymon, that's what everyone called them.
Reinout was the eldest and the strongest.
He had a shiny coat and strong legs.
He could run faster than the wind.
But the most special thing was this: when the four brothers wanted to get on his back, his back grew longer!
That way all four of them could ride Bayard at the same time.
Reinout in front and his three younger brothers behind.
And he loved the four brothers, just as they loved him.
At that time the great emperor Charlemagne ruled.
One day the four brothers had a quarrel with the emperor.
The emperor got so angry that he sent his soldiers after them.
Wherever the brothers went, the soldiers came after them.
The four brothers jumped on his back.
But the brothers grew tired of running.
They didn't want to quarrel anymore.
You must give me the horse Bayard.
That horse has always helped you escape.
I never want to see it again.
The four brothers looked at each other.
With tears in his eyes Reinout went to Bayard.
I'm sorry, my friend, he whispered.
They took Bayard to the emperor.
The emperor had a big millstone tied around Bayard's neck.
And he had him thrown into the river Scheldt.
Everyone stood on the bank watching.
Bayard was so strong that he stamped his hooves on the stones.
His head came above the water.
He swam to the other side.
And he looked at Reinout one last time.
Far away, into the big forest.
Nobody could ever catch him again.
People say Bayard still runs around there today.
And if you hear the wind neighing in the forest, maybe it's Bayard.
In the town of Dendermonde they never forget Bayard.
Every ten years there's a big festival.
They make an enormous horse out of wood and cloth.
It's as big as a house.
Twelve strong men carry it through the streets.
And on its back sit four boys.
They play the four sons of Aymon.
The whole town lines the streets.
And the big wooden horse dances through the town.
Because the horse Bayard is the pride of Dendermonde.
The horse that was too strong to drown.
